findings.explanation: docker stats reports CPU %, memory usage/limit, memory %, network I/O, block I/O and PIDs; it has no log-line rate. The write-rate severity (high_loglines_per_sec_above_2x_baseline), the drop-rate denominator and the baseline drift all depend on a metric no Docker interface emits.
findings.quote: sourcetype=docker:stats for per-container log-line write rate from docker stats style scripted or modular input with fields normalized through coalesce(loglines_per_sec, loglinesPerSec)
findings.suggested_fix: Name a real source for log-line rate, e.g. counting indexed events per container_id from the logging driver (Splunk logging driver / OTel filelog) per minute, or json-file byte growth under /var/lib/docker/containers/<id>/; otherwise drop the write-rate branch.

findings.explanation: Splunk_TA_nix ships no journald input or docker:journald / linux:journald:docker sourcetypes; its documented sourcetypes are cpu, vmstat, df, ps, top, etc. Journald is collected by the Splunk platform's native journald input (inputs.conf [journald://...]) on a universal forwarder. dataSources and implementation additionally call the collector 'Splunk Add-on for Linux', which is a different, collectd-based product (Splunkbase 3412).
findings.quote: Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux ([Splunkbase 833](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/833)) for journald and host scripted inputs
findings.suggested_fix: Say: collect docker.service journal entries with the Splunk forwarder's native journald input filtered to _SYSTEMD_UNIT=docker.service and assign sourcetype docker:journald; use Splunk_TA_nix df/df_metric (or a custom script) for the /var/lib/docker/containers filesystem.

findings.explanation: Application State has been deprecated since CIM 4.12.0 in favour of Endpoint, and it models process/service/port inventory, not log-driver delivery; the SPL uses no data model.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove Application_State (and Performance unless the filesystem arm is CIM-mapped Storage); state the detection is raw-sourcetype only.

findings.explanation: The SPL expects dockerd journal lines carrying a lines_dropped counter and 'rotating log' messages. dockerd typically logs 'Failed to log msg ... for logger' errors but json-file rotation is normally silent and non-blocking mode drops are not reported with a numeric counter, so dropped_count and rotation_cadence_per_hour may always be zero.
findings.quote: dockerd log-driver, rotation, and drop telemetry
findings.suggested_fix: Capture real dockerd journal samples for json-file rotation, ring-buffer overflow in mode=non-blocking and remote-driver failures, quote the exact message text in dataSources, and align the regex with it.

findings.explanation: 'Splunk Connect for Containers' is not a Splunk product; the real names are Splunk Connect for Docker (4496) and Splunk Connect for Kubernetes. The same name appears twice in detailedImplementation.
findings.quote: optional Splunk Connect for Containers or Splunk Connect for Docker
findings.suggested_fix: Remove 'Splunk Connect for Containers' or replace it with the Splunk OpenTelemetry Collector.

findings.explanation: Template scenarios that do not explain how this SPL produces false rows; the real causes are buried in exclusions and Step 5.
findings.quote: Synthetic probe on `host_id`, `container_id`, `th`, `]` — Health checks in `oti_containers` populate the same fields the SPL groups on.
findings.suggested_fix: List concrete causes: planned fluentd/syslog collector restarts producing connection-refused lines; dockerd message text changes after upgrades; load tests generating deliberate log bursts; containers intentionally using the none driver; new images without a baseline row falling back to fleet p99.

findings.explanation: Generator checklist residue that is also false: equipment lists five items and equipmentModels is hashicorp_terraform, which has nothing to do with log-driver health. 'returns exactly the six mandated strings' is similar residue.
findings.quote: Closing checklist: five step headers with plain em dashes, Step 3 fenced SPL matches spl field, monitoringType lists Reliability and Availability, cimModels include Application_State and Performance, equipment lists docker and linux, equipmentModels lists docker_engine and linux_journald
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the closing checklist and 'mandated' language; set equipmentModels to Docker Engine / journald models instead of hashicorp_terraform.

findings.explanation: Unnamed literature is not evidence, and the moby issue's subject is unverified; Step 5 also claims weekly exports 'satisfy most HIPAA, SOC2 CC7.2, and PCI 10.7 discussions'. status 'verified' with a generic reviewer handle overstates validation.
findings.quote: Pinterest-scale container logging engineering literature, and moby issue 45217 on non-blocking buffer behavior
findings.suggested_fix: Cite specific documents only after confirming the moby issue title, change 'satisfy' to 'support', and set status to draft pending SME review.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: Both multisearch arms contain stats (the journal arm has two); multisearch accepts only purely streaming subsearches, so the search fails. Move aggregation after the fan-in or use append.

The critical branch tests match(blocking_mode, "(?i)blocking|unknown"), which also matches 'non_blocking', so non-blocking containers raise critical_remote_driver_disconnected_blocking_mode, the opposite of the documented intent. 'timeout' also catches unrelated i/o timeout lines.
streamstats time_window=3600s runs after stats BY host_id, container_id, which removes _time, so driver_state_churn cannot be computed as a one-hour window.
toString() (camelCase) is used throughout; the Search Reference documents lowercase tostring() and states eval expressions are case-sensitive. Confirm it parses.
Uses Application_State.app and Application_State.info, which are not fields of the (deprecated) Application State model, so the tstats returns nothing.

summary: The log-driver delivery concept and the troubleshooting cases are useful, but the UC depends on a loglines_per_sec field that docker stats does not produce, credits the Unix and Linux add-on with journald collection, maps to the deprecated Application_State model with non-existent fields, and the SPL uses stats inside multisearch.
